mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts by more than 5% in the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between HOUST decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in the last two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, signals a stable monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors favor equities in low-inflationary growth environments.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between low CPIAUCSL and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising employment (PAYEMS) and falling unemployment (UNRATE) over the last month signals a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances with rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE, or the joint effect of these variables on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in the last month, coupled with a stable or decreasing unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals robust consumer demand and a healthy labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% in 1 month AND UNRATE stable/decreasing
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS increase and stable/decreasing UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% for three consecutive months, coupled with a stable or decreasing consumer price index (CPIAUCSL), signals a controlled inflation environment under tight monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors favor equities in stable, high-interest rate environments.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% for 3 months AND CPIAUCSL stable/decreasing
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and stable/decreasing CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
